transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Alex Gomez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Bluepoint CTO), Emily Santos (Product Lead), Ravi Menon (ML Engineer)

Summary:
Short PLG/self-serve discovery to understand Bluepoint's goals for integrating LLMs into product, time-to-first-token expectations, and which deployment path (hosted vs dedicated vs private) fits their security and latency needs.

Topics:
- Quickstart / free credits / time-to-first-token
- Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
- Cost vs latency, batching, KV cache, quantization
- Next steps and pilot/benchmark planning

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, and i've got priya here our systems engineer. how's it going?
[00:08] Daniel: good, thanks. we were curious about the quickstart — we want to test time-to-first-token and see how fast we can get something in prod.
[00:14] Emily: yeah also free credits you mentioned in the email, how does that work?
[00:19] Priya: so the PLG quickstart gives you an API key and a sandbox org, free credits for a month typically. time-to-first-token is often minutes — sign up, spin up model, call generate. we help with a sample prompt pack.
[00:32] Ravi: minutes sounds great but our main worry is latency for synchronous calls, and cost when we scale. looking at hosted first, but dedicated might be needed for predictable throughput.
[00:42] Alex: totally, that's the common pattern. quickstart = hosted API, fastest path. Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable throughput and isolation; Private gives you VPC or on-prem for compliance.
[00:54] Daniel: can you run a short perf benchmark during the pilot? we have 150 RPS at 256 tokens average — want to know latency p95 and cost estimates.
[01:03] Priya: yes, we can do a benchmark. quick question: how strict is your data residency and encryption reqs? e.g., need customer-managed KMS?
[01:12] Daniel: we need KMS support and audit logs for the legal team, SOC2 is required for vendor selection. SSO would be nice for the console.
[01:19] Alex: we support KMS integrations, audit logs, and SSO/SAML in Dedicated/Private. Hosted has SOC2 compliance and configurable retention; customer-managed KMS is typically for Private.
[01:30] Emily: what's the time to spin up a Dedicated pool if we decide to buy reserved capacity?
[01:35] Priya: provisioning depends on size — typically a few days to provision in our infra, might be longer for on-prem. but for evaluation we do hosted + a benchmark to validate throughput and perf.
[01:45] Ravi: earlier you mentioned KV cache — how much does that help for our use case? we do a lot of chat and long context.
[01:51] Priya: KV cache and prefix caching can reduce per-token work significantly for repeated prefixes and chat workloads; that reduces cost and improves p95 latency since it avoids recomputing keys. sometimes transcribed as KV "cash" in notes ha.
[02:04] Daniel: any gotchas with batching? we need low latency but want batch efficiency.
[02:08] Priya: balancing batching vs latency is an art — Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and latency SLOs, and you can control policy: prefer lower latency or higher throughput. for quickstart we'll show you default settings and recommendations.
[02:20] Emily: can you show an example of the API call? i looked at the SDKs but a short sample would help our engineers.
[02:26] Alex: sure, quick sample in the doc — POST to /v1/generate with model param, or use the SDK. we'll send a quickstart repo link.
[02:33] Ravi: we might also evaluate open-source stacks on our infra — some teams prefer self-hosting for cost. how does Redwood compare?
[02:40] Alex: common competitor notes: Anthropic/OpenAI for hosted simplicity; internal on-prem stacks give control but cost ops time. Redwood aims to give unified API across hosted/dedicated/private so you can transition without rework.
[02:52] Daniel: security wise, our procurement will want a security package and pen test reports. do you have an SOC2 report?
[02:58] Alex: yes, hosted environment is SOC2, and we can share SOC2 report and security docs after an NDA. Dedicated/Private have additional artefacts for compliance.
[03:09] Emily: what about data retention and logs? we need to ensure PII is not stored.
[03:14] Priya: we have configurable retention and can enable no-persist mode for sensitive workloads on Private. Hosted can be configured to not retain prompts but check the security addendum.
[03:24] Daniel: ok great. for the pilot we want: 1) free credits to run quick perf tests, 2) a short benchmark plan, 3) maybe a demo of the SDK.
[03:33] Alex: got it — next steps we'll send quickstart repo + free credits link, priya will draft a benchmark plan and we can schedule a 45 minute demo next wed.
[03:41] Ravi: timeline — we're aiming to have a POC by end of month, and then decide on dedicated vs hosted based on p95 latency and cost.
[03:49] Priya: sounds reasonable; for the benchmark we'll ask for a sample prompt set and target throughput — ravi, can you share that?
[03:55] Ravi: yes i'll drop the sample prompts and a few throughput targets to your email.
[04:01] Alex: quick note on pricing — hosted is usage-based; dedicated is monthly reserved capacity; we can run rough cost estimates once we have token counts.
[04:09] Emily: do you have any guides on quantization or token optimizations?
[04:13] Priya: yes, we have Optimize recommendations — quantization profiles and batching knobs. we'll include recommendations with the quickstart.
[04:21] Daniel: any SLA for hosted? we need uptime guarantees for prod.
[04:25] Alex: hosted has enterprise SLA options; Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and predictability. we'll include that in the materials.
[04:33] Emily: one nit — our infra team might require VPC peering for logs, is that supported?
[04:37] Priya: yes, Private or Dedicated can do VPC options and peering; on-prem requires more setup.
[04:44] Alex: ok let's recap and assign actions.
[04:47] Priya: action items: alex send quickstart + credits, priya draft benchmark, daniel share prompts.
[04:53] Daniel: will do. and please include a sample p95 latency baseline for similar customers.
[04:58] Alex: will include benchmark examples. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark demo.
[05:05] (call wraps, small crosstalk, audio noise)

End of transcript.

Recap / Notes (auto):
- Customer is evaluating Redwood as PLG/self-serve hosted path for quick evaluation; likely pilot leading to dedicated or private depending on results.
- Security requirements: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML.
- Pilot asks: free credits, benchmark run at ~150 RPS, sample prompts, latency and cost targets.
